title: A2A Vendor Core Execution Contract
description: Normalized request/response envelope for Vendor Core adapters (Arista, Cisco, Juniper, ...). This schema formalizes the response envelope already used in practice (see response_schema.py in a2a-containment-core, MIT), written as a shared convention so that the common multi-vendor UI (a2a-console) can read every vendor the same way. Two request styles are covered: the original NL-classified `/execute` path (`query` + intent-classified `route`), and the deterministic `/deploy_structured` path (`task_type` + `params`, no LLM involved) used by e.g. `a2a-interconnect`. A Vendor Core may implement either or both; the response envelope below is shared by both.

trace_id.description: Unique identifier correlating this contract instance across the init/observe/act/report lifecycle.

query.description: Natural-language instruction as entered by the operator, on the `/execute` path. Routing to read/write/diagnose is classification-driven (NL intent classification), not an explicit client-supplied operation code. Not present on the deterministic `/deploy_structured` path; use `task_type` instead.

task_type.description: Explicit, client-supplied task identifier for the deterministic `/deploy_structured` path (e.g. `interface_mtu`, `interface_ipv4`, `bgp_neighbor`, `create_vlan`). Selects a fixed, LLM-free configuration template on the Vendor Core side, as an alternative to NL-intent-classified `route`/`query`. Mutually exclusive with `query` in practice.

params.description: Structured, task_type-specific parameters for the deterministic `/deploy_structured` path (e.g. `{"interface": "et-0/0/2", "mtu": 9000}`). Present only alongside `task_type`.

route.description: The normalized operation category, independent of vendor-specific mechanism (NETCONF, eAPI, PyEZ, etc.). On the `/execute` path this is derived from NL intent classification of `query`; on the `/deploy_structured` path it is a fixed property of `task_type` (deployment tasks are `write`).

vendor_key.description: Vendor/NOS identifier (e.g. arista_ceos, juniper_ptx, cisco_nxos). Selects the Vendor Core adapter and its NOS_PROFILES entry in the shared UI.

routed_to.description: URL of the downstream agent this request was dispatched to (e.g. the vendor's NETCONF write agent).

status.description: Normalized outcome status, shared across all Vendor Core Hubs regardless of vendor. `dry_run` and `no_changes` are treated as OK outcomes (`no_changes` covers the idempotency case: the desired state was already present, so nothing was applied); `failure`/`error`/`blocked` are not.

summary.description: Short, human-readable one-line summary of the result, shown directly in the operator UI.

result.description: Vendor/route-specific inner payload on the `/execute` path (e.g. generated NETCONF XML, eAPI commands, diff output). Intentionally left open-shaped per vendor and route; the outer envelope is what is normalized, not the inner detail.

deploy_result.description: Vendor/task_type-specific inner payload on the `/deploy_structured` path. Plays the same role as `result` does on the `/execute` path (open-shaped per vendor and task_type); the two paths use different key names for this inner payload in current implementations.

human_confirmation_required.description: Reserved for a future diagnose -> approval -> execute flow. True signals the UI should show an approval prompt before proceeding.

recommended_action.description: Reserved for a future diagnose -> approval -> execute flow. A suggested corrective command, when applicable.
